title: COMP 3760 · Lecture 1
subtitle: Algorithm analysis: basic operations, counting, order of growth and big-O, preparing for Quiz 1
description: Tom Magliery's Lecture 1 (textbook 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1): what an algorithm is, find and fib, counting statements and basic operations with the tie-breakers, setting up and simplifying the sums, best/worst/average case, orders of growth, and Big-O / Big-Ω / Big-Θ. Live per-line execution counters for every slide algorithm and the quiz-style pseudocode, a loop-iteration grid, a growth-rate plot and a big-O checker. Ends with the lecture's practice problems worked, a mock quiz in the real multiple-choice format, and a study sheet.
intro:
:::quiz Quiz format, from the course intro
There are **10 or 11 main quizzes** and the **lowest score is dropped**; together they are **27%** of the grade (practice quizzes are another 5%). Each quiz **covers the most recent lecture material**. **Practice quizzes** are untimed, repeatable and open-book/notes/AI/whatever. **Main quizzes** are **one take only** (weekly deadline), **timed** and **closed-everything** (honour system): no re-takes, no late takes, no excuses. You must score at least 50% on two of the three of {Quizzes, Midterm, Final} to pass. The questions are multiple choice on short pseudocode: *is this a valid algorithm?*, *which line is the basic operation?*, *how many times is it executed?* The mock quiz at the end of this module is in exactly that format.
:::

steps.note: take it cold first to find the gaps (about 20 min)
the four parts of the definition; 'finite amount of time' is the valid-algorithm trap
the definition and the tie-breaker list; every 'which line' question comes from here
Σ1 = n, ΣΣ1 = n², Σi = n(n−1)/2, halving = log n; the 'how many times' questions
drop lower-order terms and constants; O = at most, Ω = at least, Θ = exactly
redo the lecture's three practice problems on paper before checking
the quiz is closed-book, so read it once and then reproduce it from memory
